text: Bharatiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited (BBSSL) International Year of Cooperatives (IYC) – 2025 Progress Update Report – August- 2025 Membership Growth BBSSL’s membership base continued to expand in August 2025, reflecting growing interest and engagement from Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) and other cooperative entities. The membership increased from 25121 in July 2025 to 27730 in August 2025. To further accelerate cooperative participation, BBSSL has set a target of enrolling an additional 20,000 cooperative societies during the financial year 2025–26. Significant efforts were made this month toward achieving this goal through strategic meetings and collaborative engagements. Dated: - 05.08.2025 संसदीय कायª से संबंिधत वåरķ अिधकाåरयŌ क े साथ बैठक… सहकाåरता मंýालय, नई िदÐली संसदीय कायª से संबंिधत िविभÆन िवषयŌ पर क¤ þीय सहकाåरता मंýालय क े वåरķ अिधकाåरयŌ क े साथ बैठक कì । We all have to work together! - Dr. Ashish Bhutani In the august presence of Dr. Ashish Kumar Bhutani, Secretary, Ministry of Cooperation, Government of India, Shri Chetan Joshi, Managing Director, Bharatiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited (BBSSL) and Shri Prasanna Prabhu, Chairman, Sri Sri Institute of Agricultural Science and Technology Trust (SSIAST) signed this historic Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), which marks a strategic collaboration to revive indigenous seed systems and promote natural farming. Through this partnership, BBSSL and SSIAST will conserve and promote indigenous seeds, build a strong farmer-seed bank network, conduct training and integrate digital tools for seed traceability. The collaboration aims to empower farmers, protect seed biodiversity and strengthen the goals of the National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF). On this occasion, Secretary Cooperatives Mr. Ashish Kumar Bhutani's wife Mrs. Bhutani ji, Mrs Archana ji, Mrs Bhavna ji, Mr. Pankaj Bansal ji Additional Secretary Cooperatives GOI Mr. Dinesh Kumar Verma ji Joint Secretary Cooperatives GOI and Mr. Jai Prakash Singh ji, Chief Cooperative Services BBSSL etc. were present. As part of the International Year of Cooperatives 2025 (IYC2025), BBSSL had the honour to represent India’s cooperative seed sector at a Guest Lecture Series hosted by the National Institute of Agricultural Marketing (NIAM), Jaipur, an esteemed institution under the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India. Lead by Shri Muktanand Agrawal, IAS (Director General, NIAM), Dated: - 11-12.08.2025 visit at Jaipur Meeting with Principal, Secretary Cooperative /RCS along with other officials/Officers, Seed Certification Agency- Rajasthan in reference to IYC-2025 for onboarding on PACS. Shri J P Singh (Head — Cooperative Services) and Dr Omveer (Head — Traditional Seed & Administrative Officer) were invited as Special Guest Speakers to share BBSSL’s vision, organizational framework, and strategic roadmap to strengthen India’s cooperative ecosystem. Highlights from Shri J P Singh’s Keynote Address 1. Defining Cooperatives & Their Principles — He explained that cooperatives are autonomous, member-driven organizations established to meet common economic, social, and cultural needs through democratic control, guided by the values of self-help, equity, equality, and solidarity. 2. Indigenous Roots of Cooperation — India’s cooperative spirit is deeply rooted in traditional systems like chit funds, kuris, and bhishis, aligned with the philosophy of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam (the world is one family). 3. Journey of the Cooperative Movement — Traced landmark moments including the Cooperative Credit Societies Act (1904), Community Development Programme (1951), NABARD formation (1982), MSCS Act (2002), and the establishment of the Ministry of Cooperation (2021). 4. Major Reforms by the Ministry of Cooperation — Formation of 2 lakh new PACS, modernization of existing societies, integration with CSC services, creation of national- level cooperatives such as BBSSL, NCEL, and NCOL, and introduction of the National Cooperative Policy 2025. 5. BBSSL’s Role in Seed Self-Reliance — Established in 2023 under the MSCS Act, 2002, BBSSL’s mission is to make India self-reliant in seed production, strengthen cooperative seed infrastructure, and provide farmers with certified, high-quality seeds under the Bharat Beej brand. 6. Core Functions — From accelerating seed innovation and engaging small & marginal farmers to developing seed processing facilities, building marketing networks, and promoting sustainable farming practices.
